hypothesis: Replace the short-lived Callback local with direct typed extraction of State and materialize the signed direction conversion as a named floating-point temporary. This tests whether source-level live-range creation order can give the earlier State value retail's r31 and the later target actor retail's r30 while also rotating the final conversion web into retail's f3/f1/f2 assignment.
outcome: Both changes are optimized to the same object as the preserved 99.44444% candidate. They do not repeat the prior declaration-order, state-auto, target-auto, threshold, or current-z variants, but they do not alter register allocation.
remaining_divergence: The generated object is size- and relocation-exact. GC/1.3 still assigns State to r30 and target actor to r31 while retail uses r31 and r30. In the final signed-conversion block, generated uses f2/f3/f1 for bias, threshold, and converted direction/position values while retail uses f3/f1/f2. The raw instruction diff substantiates the operand-only differences.
